From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Panne, panné, panně, and pannę

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French panne. Doublet of pen, penna, and pinna.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pæn/
  • Rhymes: -æn
  • Homophone: pan

Noun

[edit]

panne (countable and uncountable, plural pannes)

  1. A lustrous finish applied to velvet and satin.
  2. A fabric resembling velvet, but having the nap flat and less close.
  3. (ecology) A wetland consisting of a small depression, with or without standing water, often in a salt marsh or other coastal wetland.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • Penn'a, penna, Penna

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Middle French panne, from Old French penne (“fur, especially for lining garments”), from Latin pinna (“feather”). The semantic trajectory was possibly influenced by a Frankish term with the same double-sense as Middle High German vëder (“fur; feather”).

(This etymology is missing or incomplete. Please add to it, or discuss it at the Etymology scriptorium. Particularly: “How does the "breakdown" sense come into this? Confusing.”)

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pan/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Homophones: pannes, paonne, paonnes

Noun

[edit]

panne f (plural pannes)

  1. plush velvet
  2. breakdown (state of no longer functioning)
  3. purlin

Derived terms

[edit]
  • dépanner
  • en panne
  • panne sèche

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Catalan: pana
  • → German: Panne
    • → Polish: pana
  • → Italian: panne
  • → Portuguese: pane

References

[edit]
  • “panne”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Middle English

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

    Inherited from Old English panne, from Proto-West Germanic *pannā, from Proto-Germanic *pannǭ, from Late Latin panna.

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • pan, pane
    • ponne (West Midland)

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈpan(ə)/, (West Midland) /ˈpɔn(ə)/

    Noun

    [edit]

    panne (plural pannes)

    1. A pan, skillet, tin, or cookpot; any metal container used for cooking in.
    2. The head, especially its top and its contents.
    3. The harnpan or brainpan (skull)
    Derived terms
    [edit]
    • brayn panne
    • heed panne
    • herne panne
    • panne cake
    Descendants
    [edit]
    • English: pan
      • →? Irish: panna
      • → Japanese: パン
    • Scots: pan
    References
    [edit]
    • “panne, n.(1).”, in MED Online, Ann Arbor, Mich.: University of Michigan, 2007, retrieved 3 July 2018.

      Old English

      [edit]

      Etymology

      [edit]

        From Proto-West Germanic *pannā.

        Pronunciation

        [edit]
        • IPA(key): /ˈpɑn.ne/

        Noun

        [edit]

        panne f

        1. pan, frying pan
          Hū fela ǣġra wilt þū þæt iċ on þǣre pannan brǣde?
          How many eggs do you want me to fry in the pan?
          • late 12th century, Peri Didaxeon
            Hǣt þæt wīn on clǣnre pannan.
            Heat the wine in a clean pan.

        Declension

        [edit]

        Weak n-stem:

        singular plural
        nominative panne pannan
        accusative pannan pannan
        genitive pannan pannena
        dative pannan pannum

        Derived terms

        [edit]
        • brǣdpanne (“frying pan”)
        • bræġnpanne (“skull”)
        • hēafodpanne (“skull”)
        • hierstepanne (“frying pan”)

        Descendants

        [edit]
        • Middle English: panne, pan, pane, ponne (West Midland)
          • English: pan
            • →? Irish: panna
            • → Japanese: パン
          • Scots: pan
